lead_with.title: Enzymes as the missing step between synbio and chemistry
lead_with.text: NRC synbio teams build strains and pathways; chemistry teams make and modify molecules. Enzymicals bridges both with **enzyme screening, enzyme engineering and chemo-enzymatic route development** — offer to be the biocatalysis partner on joint projects.

lead_with.title: From lab result to kilos
lead_with.text: Public labs often stop at proof of concept. Enzymicals takes a biotransformation **from mg to ton scale** and can supply **recombinant enzymes** for research — useful when NRC's industry partners need scale-up.

lead_with.title: Upgrading bioresources with enzymes
lead_with.text: ACRD works on oilseeds, algae, seafood by-products and biomass waste. Selective enzymatic conversion (esterases, lipases, oxidoreductases) can turn extracts into **higher-value ingredients** — a concrete angle for a joint proposal.

person.name: Fabrice Berrué
person.text: Analytical chemist at NRC's **Aquatic and Crop Resource Development** Research Centre in **Halifax**. At the Maritimes Biological Chemistry Conference (Aug 2023, Halifax) he gave the keynote as **Research Officer and Team Lead, NRC**, on **NMR-based methods** (with chemometrics) to check the quality and safety of foods and functional ingredients — natural health products, roasted coffee, honey and pulse products. NRC has featured him for NMR analysis for the agri-food industry. LinkedIn: 1,181 followers, 500+ connections; native French, advanced English. His LinkedIn experience/education sections are empty, so earlier career and degrees are **to be confirmed**. He recently shared an NRC posting for a **Team Lead, Natural Products and Analytical team (Halifax)** — his current title may have changed (to be confirmed); the NRC facility page lists Andrew Robertson as Team Lead, Natural Products Chemistry.

company.text: The **National Research Council Canada** is the federal government's main research and technology organisation, working with industry, universities and other governments through collaborative R&D, fee-for-service work and technology licensing. Its 2026-27 plan highlights **biomanufacturing and life sciences** (including the Biologics Manufacturing Centre). The **ACRD** centre focuses on agrifood and marine biotechnology on an industrial-biotech platform; its disciplines include natural product chemistry, bioprocessing, analytical technologies, algal technologies, marine biotech and plant biotech. ACRD sites are spread across Canada, including Halifax (NPAT facilities) and Charlottetown. Business contact for ACRD: April Luong, Director, Business Development.

financials.text: **Planned spending 2026-27:** about **C$1.92B** (all NRC, incl. internal services). **Planned staff:** ~4,395 FTEs. **ACRD (evaluation 2015-16 to 2020-21):** C$30.2M revenues vs C$207.3M expenses over six years; 205 staff (Jan 2022). No funding rounds — NRC is publicly funded and earns revenue from industry collaborations and fee-for-service. Budget for buying outside enzyme services is **to be confirmed**; a realistic path is joint projects (NRC programs, partner-funded work) rather than a direct purchase.

industry.title: Bioresource upgrading needs selective chemistry
